desc:
Simulate a first-in-first-out queue of integers that supports three operations. Each operation is a pair [type, value]:

  • [1, x] adds x at the back of the queue.
  • [2, 0] removes the element at the front of the queue.
  • [3, 0] reports the largest value currently in the queue.

Return the answers of all type 3 operations in the order they occur. The queue is never empty when a type 2 or type 3 operation is executed, and the input contains at least one type 3 operation. Every operation should take amortized O(1) time.

ops = [[1,3],[1,1],[3,0],[2,0],[3,0],[1,5],[3,0],[2,0],[3,0]]
queue [3,1] -> max 3;  pop 3 -> [1] -> max 1;  push 5 -> [1,5] -> max 5
pop 1 -> [5] -> max 5
result = [3, 1, 5, 5]
constraints: ops[i] = [type, value] with type in {1, 2, 3}; value is 0 for types 2 and 3
Type 2 and type 3 operations only occur on a non-empty queue
hints: Calling max() on the queue contents for every query is O(n) per query.
When a large value is pushed, every smaller value that is already in the queue (and was pushed earlier) can never be the maximum again: it leaves the queue before the large one does.

Keep a second deque holding a non-increasing sequence of values. On push, pop smaller values off its back first. On pop, if the removed value equals the front of this deque, remove that front too. The front is the maximum.
editorial: Besides the real queue, keep a deque best of values in non-increasing order. When x is pushed, every smaller value at the back of best is dominated: it is older than x and smaller, so it will be removed from the queue first and can never be the maximum. Pop those values, then append x.

The maximum is always best[0]. When the real queue pops a value v, v is also best[0] exactly when it was the maximum (equal values stay in best because only strictly smaller values are removed), so in that case pop the front of best too. Every value enters and leaves each deque once: O(1) amortized per operation, O(n) space. The same structure is what makes the sliding window maximum run in linear time.
